name: Spring Bean Scopes
overview: Should everyone share one bean, or does each request get its own? Choose a scope by deciding who shares it and when it should disappear.

sections.title: Choose who shares the bean
sections.content: Singleton gives one instance per bean definition per container. Prototype creates a new instance for each lookup or resolution. Spring does not manage prototype destruction.

images.caption: The scope controls who shares an instance and when it is created.

sections.title: Choose how long web state lives
sections.content: Request scope lasts one HTTP request. Session scope lasts one HTTP session. Application scope shares the instance across one ServletContext.

sections.title: Match scope to state
sections.content: A stateless service usually fits singleton scope. Keep request data in request scope and session data in session scope. Shared mutable state needs a thread-safety plan.

keyPoints: Choose scopes for a stateless service, one request's data, and a shopping cart. Explain who shares each instance and for how long.

interviewQA.question: Does injecting a prototype into a singleton create a new instance every call?
interviewQA.answer: Ordinary direct injection resolves it once at injection time. Use a provider or another lookup strategy if you need fresh instances.

interviewQA.question: Which scope fits an HTTP request’s data?
interviewQA.answer: Request scope gives each request its own instance.
